process_lifecycle.first_restart_attempt_result: STALE -- supervisorctl restart alone respawned the child process but did NOT reload supervisord's in-memory config from the edited file. process_lifecycle.root_cause: supervisorctl restart <program> does not imply a config reread; the running supervisord daemon (PID 35283, running since 08:58AM, long before this edit) needed an explicit `supervisorctl reread` + `supervisorctl update <program>` to pick up the file change.
process_lifecycle.corrective_action: ran `supervisorctl reread` (reported 'creator_funding_worker: changed'), then `supervisorctl update creator_funding_worker` (reported 'stopped' then 'updated process group') -- this correctly targeted ONLY creator_funding_worker, not a bare `update` that could have touched every changed program.

part14_v2_short_window_growth_estimate.label: BOUNDED_SHORT_WINDOW_GROWTH_ESTIMATE
part14_v2_short_window_growth_estimate.important_nuance: this short-window rate is NOT the sustained/guaranteed long-term rate. daily_payload_cap_bytes (1 GiB) is an IN-PROCESS counter (self._payload_bytes, reset to 0 on every process start, not a true rolling calendar-day counter) that hard-refuses full-payload writes once exceeded, falling back to the tiny hot-payload representation for all subsequent observations in that process lifetime. At the observed rate (~26.7 MB in ~25 minutes since restart), the process would take multiple hours of continuous full-payload writes to reach the 1 GiB in-process cap, and would then degrade to hot-only rather than fail. The cap is real and enforced (verified with 9 passing tests including a real-write test), but this short window alone does not prove the cap will bind before a future process restart resets the counter -- that is an inherent property of the current implementation, not a gap introduced by this cutover, and is recorded here rather than glossed over.

part15_replay_evidence_check.method: bounded, read-only inspection of the most recent V2 rows written by live production traffic since cutover (not a broad replay run)

verdict_note: Cutover succeeded. Legacy retained_acquisition.db growth is arrested (zero byte change across all post-cutover measurements, mtime frozen). RetainedAcquisitionStoreV2 is confirmed receiving new retention (883 new rows, 26.7 MB, since process restart) with full replay-required evidence fields intact and zero write failures. Active process environment was verified directly (not just file contents), confirming legacy=OFF, bounded=ON, no dual-write. One real corrective action was required and is fully disclosed: the first restart attempt did not apply the config change (supervisord's in-memory state was stale until `reread`+`update` were run); this was caught by the explicit Part 11 verification step rather than assumed successful, and resolved narrowly (targeting only creator_funding_worker). B2N remains frozen at exactly 1/20 with all three live artifact digests byte-identical before and after. No rollback conditions triggered. Legacy 61.3+ GB DB was not deleted, modified, VACUUMed, or checkpointed -- it is now historical/read-only pending a separate future RA4-C5 archival/retirement milestone.
